display_contract.front: Arabic script only; no translation, English question, transliteration, definition, or hint.
display_contract.back: All translations, definitions, examples, grammar/register data, metadata, and eight layered fields.
display_contract.retrieval_direction: Arabic -> meaning/use first; alternate representations are scheduled separately.

source_basis.note: ArabicPod101 Newbie Lesson 3 teaches basic self-introduction. The lesson is presented as Standard Arabic while noting that its sample dialogue is informal in register.

cards.title: أَنَا
cards.definition_ar: ضَمِيرُ المُتَكَلِّمِ المُفْرَدِ، يَسْتَعْمِلُهُ الرَّجُلُ وَالمَرْأَةُ.
cards.definition_en: The first-person singular pronoun ‘I’; the same form is used by male and female speakers.

layers.concept_expansion: Arabic can place أَنَا directly before a name, noun, or adjective in a present-time nominal sentence without an explicit present-tense verb ‘to be.’
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not add a separate present-tense equivalent of English ‘am’ in simple nominal sentences such as أَنَا طَالِب.
layers.transfer_prompt: Introduce yourself using أَنَا followed by your name or role.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize أَنَا in audio and use it automatically to begin simple self-statements.

cards.title: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ / مَا اسْمُكِ؟

translations.ur: آپ کا نام کیا ہے؟ / آپ کا نام کیا ہے؟

cards.definition_ar: سُؤالٌ عَنِ الاِسْمِ؛ ـكَ لِمُخاطَبٍ مُذَكَّرٍ وَـكِ لِمُخاطَبَةٍ مُؤَنَّثَةٍ.
cards.definition_en: A question asking someone’s name; use -ka for one male addressee and -ki for one female addressee.
cards.example_en: Hello, what is your name? (to a woman)

layers.direct_answer: To a man: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ To a woman: مَا اسْمُكِ؟
layers.concept_expansion: مَا means ‘what’; اسْم means ‘name’; the attached endings ـكَ and ـكِ mean ‘your’ for a male or female addressee.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ — اِسْمِي عَلِي. / مَا اسْمُكِ؟ — اِسْمِي لَيْلَى.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: The written forms may look identical without vowel marks, but the final vowel of the suffix changes with the addressee’s gender.
layers.connections_and_memory: This is the same ـكَ / ـكِ gender contrast already encountered in كَيْفَ حالُكَ؟ / كَيْفَ حالُكِ؟
layers.transfer_prompt: Ask one man and one woman their names, changing only the correct suffix.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce both versions without hesitation and hear the -ka/-ki contrast in speech.

cards.title: اِسْمِي
cards.definition_ar: اِسْمٌ مَعَ ياءِ المُتَكَلِّمِ، وَمَعْناهُ «اِسْمِي / my name».
cards.definition_en: The noun ‘name’ with the first-person possessive suffix -ī: ‘my name.’

layers.direct_answer: اِسْمِي = my name / my name is ...
layers.concept_expansion: The ending ـي marks first-person possession here: اسْم + ـي → اِسْمِي.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Arabic does not require an explicit present-tense ‘is’ in اِسْمِي مُحَمَّد.
layers.connections_and_memory: Compare اِسْمِي ‘my name’ with اسْمُكَ / اسْمُكِ ‘your name.’
layers.transfer_prompt: Answer the name question with your actual name using اِسْمِي.
layers.mastery_evidence: Respond to مَا اسْمُكَ؟ or مَا اسْمُكِ؟ immediately with اِسْمِي + name.

cards.title: طَالِب / طَالِبَة
cards.definition_ar: طَالِبٌ لِلذَّكَرِ وَطَالِبَةٌ لِلأُنْثَى؛ شَخْصٌ يَدْرُسُ في مَدْرَسَةٍ أَو جامِعَةٍ.
cards.definition_en: A person who studies; طالب is masculine and طالبة is feminine.
cards.example_en: I am a male student. / I am a female student.

layers.direct_answer: طَالِب = male student; طَالِبَة = female student.
layers.concept_expansion: The feminine form adds ة, a very common feminine noun marker. Both can follow أَنَا directly in a present-time nominal sentence.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not assume every feminine noun ends in ة or every noun ending in ة follows a simple masculine/feminine pair; this card teaches this specific productive pair.
layers.connections_and_memory: The root ط-ل-ب relates to seeking/requesting; a طالب is literally one who seeks, conventionally a student.
layers.transfer_prompt: Say ‘I am a student’ using the form appropriate to the speaker.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize and produce both gender forms and use them correctly after أَنَا.

cards.title: أَنَا أَيْضًا
cards.definition_ar: تَعْبيرٌ يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلقَوْلِ إِنَّ الشَّيْءَ نَفْسَهُ يَنْطَبِقُ عَلَى المُتَكَلِّمِ.
cards.definition_en: A response meaning that the same statement also applies to the speaker: ‘me too.’

layers.direct_answer: أَنَا أَيْضًا = me too / I also do or am.
layers.concept_expansion: أَيْضًا adds the meaning ‘also/too’; the phrase is useful as a short conversational response.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: The phrase is not limited to being a student; it can respond whenever the same statement applies to you.
layers.transfer_prompt: Someone says a fact that is also true of you; answer naturally in Arabic.
layers.mastery_evidence: Use أَنَا أَيْضًا spontaneously as a short agreement response.

cards.title: حَقًّا
cards.definition_ar: ظَرْفٌ أَو تَعْبيرٌ لِلتَّأْكِيدِ أَو لإِظْهارِ الدَّهْشَةِ: «فِعْلًا؟ / حَقًّا؟».
cards.definition_en: An adverb meaning ‘really/truly,’ also used as a short response showing surprise or confirmation.

layers.concept_expansion: It can intensify a statement or stand alone as a reaction meaning ‘Really?’
layers.worked_or_physical_example: حَقًّا؟ أَنَا أَيْضًا. — Really? Me too.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not confuse the conversational reaction حَقًّا؟ with the noun حَقّ ‘right/truth,’ though they share the same root.
layers.connections_and_memory: The root ح-ق-ق carries ideas of truth, reality, and rightness.
layers.transfer_prompt: React with surprise when someone tells you something unexpected.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize حَقًّا in connected speech and use it naturally as ‘really?’ or ‘truly.’
